sandhi.note: सः loses its visarga before the consonant ch; the resulting short a then doubles the ch (स + छिन्न → सच्छिन्न). The Gita Press prints the two words together.
-aḥ before the voiced h becomes -o, twice. Inside हताश्वः, हत + अश्व → हताश्व (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः, 6.1.101).
The augment a- stands between prefix and root; i before it becomes y (अभि + अ-धावत → अभ्यधावत).
-aḥ + a- → -o’-: the visarga becomes u, a + u → o, and the following a is absorbed (avagraha).

samasa.vigraha: खड्गः च चर्म च खड्गचर्म (samāhāra dvandva); खड्गचर्म धरति इति खड्गचर्मधरः
samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa containing a samāhāra dvandva
samasa.alt: The first member could also be an itaretara dvandva (खड्गचर्मणी, ‘sword and shield’); 3.31 has the singular खड्गचर्मणा, which supports the samāhāra reading.

morph.note: Imperfect ātmanepada of √धाव्, which takes both voices (धावति / धावते). The augment अ- comes after the prefix: अभि-अ-धावत.
Nominative singular of the an-stem छिन्नधन्वन् (n dropped, a lengthened: -धन्वा, like राजा). See 3.5 for the replacement of धनुस् by धन्वन्.

mantras.anvaya: छिन्नधन्वा विरथः हताश्वः हतसारथिः खड्गचर्मधरः सः असुरः तां देवीम् अभ्यधावत।
mantras.anvaya_en: One subject (सः … असुरः) carrying five predicate adjectives — four bahuvrīhis of loss and one of arms — and the verb अभ्यधावत with its object.
mantras.lit: He, with bow cut, chariotless, horses slain, charioteer slain, rushed at that Goddess, the asura holding sword and shield.
mantras.tr: Bow broken, chariot gone, horses and charioteer slain, the asura took up sword and shield and charged at the Goddess.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Took up’ renders the compound खड्गचर्मधरः ‘bearing sword and shield’ as an action.

comm.t: The line of four bahuvrīhis sums up 3.4–5: everything a chariot-warrior fights with is gone. Cikṣura goes on, on foot.
The Purāṇa honours the courage of the asura generals even as they fall; none of them flees.

samasa.literal: by (a sword) whose edge is sharp
samasa.alt: As the last member of a masculine bahuvrīhi, धारा shortens its ā (-धार).

morph.note: Absolutive of आ + √हन् with ल्यप्: the root’s nasal drops and t is added before -य (आ-हत्-य).
Perfect of √हन् with आ (see जघान, 3.4). With the accusative of the person and the locative of the part: ‘struck the Goddess on the left arm’.
Nominative singular of a -वत् stem: -वान्. वेगवत् ‘possessing speed’.

mantras.anvaya: (सः) अतिवेगवान् तीक्ष्णधारेण खड्गेन सिंहं मूर्धनि आहत्य देवीम् अपि सव्ये भुजे आजघान।
mantras.anvaya_en: Absolutive clause with its own locative of the part (सिंहं मूर्धनि आहत्य), then the main clause on the same pattern (देवीं सव्ये भुजे आजघान).
mantras.lit: Having struck the lion on the head with his sharp-edged sword, he, very swift, struck the Goddess too on the left arm.
mantras.tr: Moving with great speed, he struck the lion on the head with his keen-edged sword, and then struck the Goddess herself on her left arm.

comm.t: Cikṣura attacks both the mount and its rider. The lion is the Goddess’s vāhana, given to her by Himavat (2.29), and a fighter in its own right (2.51–52, 3.14–16).

sandhi.note: Before kh the visarga stays; खड्गः before the voiced bh becomes खड्गो.
सः drops its visarga before k; the t of कोपात् becomes d before the vowel a.

morph.note: Perfect of √फल्: reduplication प- (ph → p) and vṛddhi in the 3rd singular (प-फाल). ‘Burst into pieces’.
Perfect of √ग्रह्: the reduplicated syllable takes samprasāraṇa and g → j (ज-ग्राह).
Absolutive of प्र + √आप्; its subject is the sword: ‘having reached her arm, the sword burst’.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) नृपनन्दन, खड्गः तस्याः भुजं प्राप्य पफाल। ततः कोपात् अरुणलोचनः सः शूलं जग्राह।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two sentences: the sword as subject of an absolutive and of पफाल; then Cikṣura as subject of जग्राह. The vocative interrupts the narrative.
mantras.lit: Reaching her arm, the sword shattered, O son of a king. Then he, red-eyed with anger, seized a spear.
mantras.tr: The sword shattered as it met her arm, O prince. Then, his eyes red with rage, he seized a spear.

comm.t: The sword breaks on the Goddess’s arm — she is not wounded. Medhas’s vocative नृपनन्दन recalls the frame: the battle is a story told to King Suratha.
Weapons breaking against the Goddess is a recurring sign in the battle books that no created weapon reaches her.

samasa.vigraha: भद्रा च असौ काली च, तस्याम्

morph.note: Intensive (yaṅ) participle: reduplication with a long vowel (जा-ज्वल्-य-) and ātmanepada -मान. ‘Blazing again and again, flaring’.
Perfect of √क्षिप्: reduplication चि- (kṣ → c) and guṇa i → e. With the locative of the target: ‘hurled at Bhadrakālī’.
Instrumental plural of the s-stem तेजस्: the s becomes o before -भिः (तेजस् + भिः → तेजोभिः).

mantras.anvaya: ततः च महासुरः तेजोभिः जाज्वल्यमानं तत् (शूलं) तु, अम्बरात् रविबिम्बम् इव, भद्रकाल्यां चिक्षेप।
mantras.anvaya_en: Main clause (महासुरः तत् भद्रकाल्यां चिक्षेप) with a participle and a simile describing the object.
mantras.lit: And then the great asura hurled it, blazing fiercely with radiance like the sun’s disc from the sky, at Bhadrakālī.
mantras.tr: Then the great asura hurled the spear at Bhadrakālī, flaming with light like the sun’s disc falling from the sky.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Falling’ is supplied to complete the simile with अम्बरात् ‘from the sky’.

comm.t: The spear is thrown, blazing like the sun. Here the narrator names the Goddess Bhadrakālī, the ‘auspicious Kālī’; the name returns at 4.39, when she vanishes after granting the gods’ boon.

morph.note: Present participle of आ + √पत्, neuter accusative singular: ‘(the spear) flying towards (her)’.
Imperfect of √मुच्, which takes a nasal in the present system (मुञ्च-). The ātmanepada form is used here; the active would be अमुञ्चत्.
शतधा नीतम् ‘brought to a hundred parts’: the passive participle stands as the verb, with the agent in the instrumental (तेन). For स च महासुरः the same verb is understood in the masculine (नीतः).

mantras.anvaya: देवी तत् आपतत् शूलं दृष्ट्वा शूलम् अमुञ्चत। तेन तत् शूलं शतधा नीतम्, सः महासुरः च (शतधा नीतः)।
mantras.anvaya_en: First sentence: absolutive and main verb. Second: a passive participle as verb, with an elliptical second subject whose participle is supplied.
mantras.lit: Seeing that spear flying at (her), the Goddess hurled a spear. By it that spear was brought to a hundred pieces, and (so was) the great asura.
mantras.tr: Seeing the spear flying at her, the Goddess hurled her own. It shattered his spear into a hundred pieces — and the great asura with it.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Her own’ and ‘his’ distinguish the two spears; ‘with it’ renders the elliptical स च महासुरः.

comm.t: Cikṣura’s death is told in three words, स च महासुरः, with the verb left to be supplied. 3.11 confirms it: हते तस्मिन् ‘when he was slain’.
The Goddess answers each weapon with its like — arrow with arrow, spear with spear — and hers prevails.
